content: I'm migrating my smart home from a mix of WiFi devices to Zigbee. The WiFi stuff is unreliable — the smart plugs drop off the network every few days and I have to power cycle them. Plus they're all phoning home to different cloud services.

Zigbee is much more reliable for home automation. It forms a mesh network where devices route through each other, so the network self-heals. And with a local coordinator like ZHA or Zigbee2MQTT in Home Assistant, everything stays local — no cloud dependency.

I'm going with Zigbee2MQTT because it gives me more control over the device pairing and configuration. Running it on the same Raspberry Pi as Home Assistant with a Sonoff Zigbee coordinator. The thing is, I want to keep my existing MQTT broker since I already have ESPHome sensors publishing to it.

Zigbee2MQTT publishes device states to MQTT topics, so it integrates perfectly with your existing broker. Your ESPHome sensors and Zigbee devices would all be on the same MQTT bus, which simplifies your automations.

Exactly — unified message bus, single source of truth for device state. I have about 30 ESPHome sensors already — temperature, humidity, motion, door contacts. Adding Zigbee gives me the smart plugs and light switches without the cloud dependency.
That's a solid architecture. ESPHome for custom sensors where you need specific hardware, Zigbee for commercial devices. All communicating over MQTT with Home Assistant as the orchestration layer.

And the Zigbee mesh means I don't need to worry about WiFi range for the smart plugs in the garage and basement. Every mains-powered Zigbee device acts as a router, so the mesh extends itself. Fundamentally it's the same topology as a service mesh — each node routes for others.

The analogy works well. Like Envoy sidecars routing traffic, Zigbee routers forward messages for devices that can't reach the coordinator directly. Battery-powered devices (end devices) are like lightweight clients that connect through the nearest router.

Ha, I'm going to start calling my smart plugs 'sidecar proxies' and see if my wife notices. Anyway — I need to figure out the MQTT topic structure for the Zigbee devices so they're consistent with my ESPHome naming convention.
